Option A working capital ko ignore karta hai. Option D payables ke badhne ko bhi ghata deta hai (sign ulta, 50). Option B depreciation add-back bhool jaata hai.

weeks.title: Management Accounting: Cost Behaviour, Contribution and Break-even
weeks.summary: Is week aap costs ko fixed/variable aur direct/indirect mein classify karna, high-low method se mixed cost todna, contribution margin, break-even, margin of safety, target profit, operating leverage aur multi-product break-even nikaalna seekhoge.
concepts: **Management vs financial accounting**: financial accounting bahar ke users (investors, lenders, tax) ke liye rules (Ind AS) ke hisaab se past report karta hai. Management accounting andar ke decisions ke liye hai: pricing, product mix, budget, make-or-buy. Yahan koi fixed format nahi; jo decision ke liye relevant ho wahi numbers. Analyst ka zyada kaam isi side hota hai.

**Cost behaviour**: **variable cost** volume ke saath badhta hai (raw material, packaging, sales commission); **fixed cost** ek relevant range mein volume se nahi badalta (rent, salaried staff, software licence); **mixed (semi-variable)** dono ka mix (electricity: fixed connection charge + per-unit usage). Per unit dekho to ulta: variable cost per unit constant, fixed cost per unit volume badhne par girta hai.

**Direct vs indirect**: direct cost kisi cost object (product, customer, branch) se seedha trace hota hai (us product ka material); indirect (overhead) kai objects mein share hota hai aur allocate karna padta hai (factory manager ki salary). Direct/indirect aur fixed/variable alag sawaal hain: product line ke supervisor ki salary direct bhi hai aur fixed bhi.

**High-low method**: mixed cost ko todne ka simple tareeka: variable rate = (highest activity par cost − lowest activity par cost) ÷ (activity ka farak); fixed part = total cost − variable rate × activity. Analyst sab data points par linear regression se bhi yahi karta hai (slope = variable rate, intercept = fixed), jo outliers se kam prabhavit hota hai.

**Contribution margin (CM)**: CM per unit = price − variable cost per unit; CM ratio = CM ÷ price. Har bechi gayi unit pehle fixed costs cover karti hai, phir profit deti hai. Profit = units × CM − fixed costs.

**Break-even aur target profit**: break-even units = fixed costs ÷ CM per unit; break-even revenue = fixed costs ÷ CM ratio. Target profit ke liye units = (fixed costs + target profit) ÷ CM. **Margin of safety** = (actual sales − break-even sales) ÷ actual sales: sales kitne % gir sakte hain loss se pehle.

**Operating leverage**: DOL = total contribution ÷ operating profit (EBIT). Sales x% badhe to EBIT lagbhag DOL × x% badhta hai (CM ratio aur fixed cost same rahein to exactly). High fixed cost business (software, airlines) ka DOL zyada: upside mein profit tezi se badhta hai, downside mein tezi se girta hai. DOL = 1 ÷ margin of safety.

**Multi-product break-even**: sales mix ko ek 'bundle' maano (jaise 3 A + 2 B), bundle ka CM nikaalo, fixed costs ÷ bundle CM = bundles, phir mix se units. Mix badla to break-even bhi badlega; products ka simple average CM lena galat hai jab mix barabar na ho.

example.problem: Fictional 'Dhaara Water Purifiers' ek purifier ₹12,000 mein bechti hai; variable cost ₹7,200 per unit; monthly fixed costs ₹48 lakh. Is mahine 1,250 units bikne ka forecast hai. CM, break-even, profit, margin of safety aur DOL nikaalo.
steps: Break-even units = 48,00,000 ÷ 4,800 = 1,000 units; break-even revenue = 48,00,000 ÷ 0.40 = ₹1.2 crore.
1,250 units par total contribution = 1,250 × 4,800 = ₹60 lakh; profit = 60 − 48 = ₹12 lakh.
Matlab: sales 10% badhe to profit lagbhag 50% badhega; sales 20% gire to break-even.
Answer: **CM ₹4,800 (40%), BEP 1,000 units, profit ₹12 lakh, MoS 20%, DOL 5**.

mistakes: Fixed cost per unit ko variable cost maan kar decisions lena. 1,000 units par ₹4,800 per unit fixed lag raha hai, par 1,250 par sirf ₹3,840; per-unit fixed number volume badalne par badalta hai.
Break-even ke liye fixed cost ko price se divide karna. Har unit sirf apna contribution (price − variable cost) fixed cost ki taraf deti hai.
Multi-product mein products ke CM ka simple average lena jab sales mix barabar na ho. Mix ke weights se bundle CM nikaalo.
revision: CM = price − VC; CM ratio = CM ÷ price.
BEP units = FC ÷ CM; BEP revenue = FC ÷ CM ratio.
Target units = (FC + target profit) ÷ CM.
High-low: VC rate = Δcost ÷ Δactivity; FC = cost − rate × activity.
DOL = contribution ÷ EBIT = 1 ÷ MoS.
Multi-product: bundle CM se break-even, phir mix se units.

questions.question: Fictional company 'Sona Biscuits' sirf ek product banaati hai. Har packet par lagne wala wrapper (packaging material) kaunsa cost hai?
questions.explanation: Har packet ke saath wrapper ka kharch badhta hai (variable) aur seedha us product se trace hota hai (direct): option B. Option C trap hai: direct cost ka matlab fixed nahi; direct/indirect traceability ka sawaal hai, fixed/variable volume ke saath behaviour ka. Factory rent jaisa cost fixed aur indirect hota.

questions.question: Fictional 'Kanak Bags' ek bag ₹500 mein bechta hai; variable cost ₹300 per bag aur monthly fixed costs ₹4,00,000 hain. Break-even ke liye har mahine kitne bags bechne honge?
questions.explanation: CM = 500 − 300 = ₹200 per bag. Break-even = 4,00,000 ÷ 200 = 2,000 bags, option C (revenue ₹10 lakh). Option A fixed cost ko price se divide karta hai, jaise poora price fixed cost cover karta ho. Option B variable cost se divide karta hai.

questions.question: Fictional factory 'Shilpa Castings' ka electricity bill 2,000 machine hours wale mahine mein ₹58,000 aur 5,000 machine hours wale mahine mein ₹1,03,000 tha (ye lowest aur highest activity months hain). High-low method se monthly fixed part kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Variable rate = (1,03,000 − 58,000) ÷ (5,000 − 2,000) = 45,000 ÷ 3,000 = ₹15 per hour. Fixed = 58,000 − 15 × 2,000 = ₹28,000 (check: 1,03,000 − 75,000 = ₹28,000), option A. Option B low month ka poora bill fixed maan leta hai. Option C cost ka farak hai, jo variable part ka hai. Option D low month ka variable part (15 × 2,000) hai.

questions.question: Fictional 'Arya Fitness Bands' ka price ₹1,200, variable cost ₹750 per unit aur fixed costs ₹9,00,000 hain. ₹4,50,000 profit kamaane ke liye kitni units bechni hongi?
questions.explanation: CM = 1,200 − 750 = ₹450. Units = (9,00,000 + 4,50,000) ÷ 450 = 13,50,000 ÷ 450 = 3,000, option D. Option A sirf break-even hai (target profit bhool gaye). Option B sirf profit ko CM se divide karta hai (fixed cost bhool gaye). Option C CM ki jagah price se divide karta hai.

questions.question: Fictional SaaS company 'Lekha Books' ka total contribution ₹30 lakh aur operating profit (EBIT) ₹6 lakh hai. Price, variable cost per unit aur fixed costs same rehte hue sales volume 10% badhta hai. Naya EBIT kitna hoga?
questions.explanation: DOL = 30 ÷ 6 = 5. Sales 10% badhe to EBIT 5 × 10% = 50% badhega: ₹9 lakh, option C. Seedha check: contribution ₹33 lakh, fixed costs ₹24 lakh same, EBIT ₹9 lakh. Option A EBIT ko bhi sirf 10% badhaata hai (operating leverage bhool gaye). Option B nayi contribution hai, EBIT nahi.

questions.question: Fictional 'Rasoi Appliances' do products bechti hai, sales mix 3 mixers : 2 grinders. Mixer: price ₹400, variable cost ₹250. Grinder: price ₹600, variable cost ₹420. Monthly fixed costs ₹8,10,000 hain. Is mix par break-even ke liye kitne mixers aur grinders bechne honge?
questions.explanation: CM: mixer ₹150, grinder ₹180. Bundle (3 mixers + 2 grinders) ka CM = 3 × 150 + 2 × 180 = ₹810. Bundles = 8,10,000 ÷ 810 = 1,000, yaani 3,000 mixers aur 2,000 grinders, option B. Option C dono CM ka simple average (165) leta hai, jo 3:2 mix ko ignore karta hai. Option A har product se alag-alag poora fixed cost cover karwata hai. Option D 1,000 bundles ko har product ki 1,000 units samajh leta hai.

weeks.title: The B2B Selling Process in Seven Steps, Measured with Data
weeks.summary: Is week aap B2B professional selling ke saat steps (prospecting se after-sales tak) samjhoge, aur har step ko funnel conversion, weighted pipeline, pipeline coverage aur ROI/payback jaise numbers se measure aur plan karna seekhoge.
concepts: **1. Prospecting aur qualifying**: ideal customer profile (industry, size, use case) se leads dhoondho, phir qualify karo ki pursue karne layak hain ya nahi. Common framework **BANT**: Budget, Authority (decision power), Need, Timeline. Analyst yahan lead scoring model banata hai: kaunse attributes historically wins se jude hain.

**2. Pre-approach aur approach**: meeting se pehle account research (annual report, news, tech stack, DMU map), phir pehla contact jo credibility banaye: customer ke business ki baat, apne product ki nahi. Achha opening ek specific, researched observation hota hai.

**3. Needs analysis**: open questions (SPIN: Situation, Problem, Implication, Need-payoff) aur active listening se pain point aur uska ₹ impact samjho. Jo problem quantify nahi hui, uske liye budget bhi nahi niklega.

**4. Offer / presentation**: generic demo nahi, customer ki needs se map kiya hua solution. **FAB**: Feature (product kya hai: 'real-time GPS tracking'), Advantage (woh kya karta hai: 'delays turant dikhte hain'), Benefit (customer ko kya milta hai: 'late-delivery penalty ₹12 lakh saal kam'). B2B mein value ko ROI, TCO aur payback period mein dikhao.

**5. Objection handling aur negotiation**: objection ko signal maano, rejection nahi. Process: listen → acknowledge → clarify (asli concern kya hai) → respond (evidence, case study, TCO) → confirm. Price objection par discount dene se pehle value dikhao; concession doge to badle mein kuch lo (longer contract, faster payment, case study rights).

**6. Closing**: buying signals (implementation timeline ke sawaal, legal review) par close karo. Techniques: trial close ('kya ye approach aapki team ke liye kaam karega?'), summary close (agreed benefits recap karke next step), alternative-choice close (Q1 ya Q2 start?). Close ka matlab clear next step aur commitment hai.

**7. Follow-up aur after-sales**: onboarding, adoption tracking, quarterly business reviews, aur renewal/upsell. B2B revenue ka bada hissa existing accounts se aata hai, isliye net revenue retention aur churn yahan ke KPIs hain.

**Sales analytics**: funnel conversion har stage par (stage-to-stage %), overall win rate, average deal size, sales cycle length, **weighted pipeline** = Σ (deal value × stage probability), aur **pipeline coverage** = pipeline ÷ quota (zaroori coverage ≈ 1 ÷ historical win rate). Target se ulta chal kar (back-solve) har stage ka zaroori volume nikaalo.

example.problem: Fictional 'Setu Logistics Software' ke pichhle quarter ka funnel: 2,000 leads → 400 qualified → 160 discovery meetings → 60 proposals → 15 wins. Agle quarter 24 wins chahiye (same conversion rates). Average deal ₹8 lakh hai. Plan banao.
steps: Overall lead-to-win = 15 ÷ 2,000 = 0.75%.
Back-solve: proposals = 24 ÷ 0.25 = 96; meetings = 96 ÷ 0.375 = 256; qualified = 256 ÷ 0.40 = 640; leads = 640 ÷ 0.20 = 3,200.
Bookings = 24 × ₹8 lakh = ₹1.92 crore.
Alternative: agar proposal-to-win 25% se 30% ho jaaye (better offer, objection handling), to 2,000 leads se hi 2,000 × 0.20 × 0.40 × 0.375 × 0.30 = 18 wins.
Answer: same rates par **3,200 leads** chahiye; ya lead volume ke saath late-stage conversion sudhaarne ka plan banao.

mistakes: Weighted pipeline ki jagah total (unweighted) pipeline ko forecast maan lena. Har deal ko uski stage probability se multiply karo.
Pipeline coverage ko 'quota se zyada hai to theek' samajhna. Zaroori coverage win rate par depend karta hai: 25% win rate par quota ka ~4 guna pipeline chahiye.
Price objection aate hi discount de dena. Pehle clarify karo ki concern budget hai, value hai ya competitor comparison; phir TCO/ROI se respond karo aur concession ke badle kuch lo.
revision: Steps: prospect → approach → needs → offer → objections/negotiation → close → after-sales.
BANT: Budget, Authority, Need, Timeline.
FAB: Feature, Advantage, Benefit (customer ka gain).
Weighted pipeline = Σ value × probability.
Needed pipeline = quota ÷ win rate.
Payback = one-time cost ÷ net annual saving.

questions.question: Fictional CRM vendor ka sales rep ek lead se poochta hai ki budget approved hai ya nahi, final decision kaun lega, kya problem hai aur kab tak solution chahiye. Ye kaam selling process ke kis step ka hai?
questions.explanation: Budget, Authority, Need, Timeline (BANT) check karna lead ko qualify karna hai, jo prospecting aur qualifying step ka hissa hai, option C. Option A trap hai kyunki ye bhi shuruaati conversation hai, par approach ka goal rapport aur credibility hai, filter karna nahi. Closing aur follow-up baad ke steps hain.

questions.question: Fictional accounting software ka salesperson kehta hai: "Isse aapki finance team ke har hafte 6 ghante manual reconciliation mein bachenge." FAB framework mein ye statement kya hai?
questions.explanation: Ye customer ko milne wala concrete gain (team ka time) bata raha hai, isliye benefit, option A. Feature product ki property hoti ('automatic bank-feed matching') aur advantage feature kya karta hai ('entries khud match hoti hain'). Option C sabse common trap hai kyunki advantage aur benefit paas-paas hain; farak ye hai ki benefit customer ke business result ki baat karta hai.

questions.question: Fictional HR-tech company 'Kaam Sathi' ke pichhle quarter mein 1,500 leads se 300 qualified, 90 proposals aur 30 wins hue. Same conversion rates par agle quarter 45 wins ke liye kitne leads chahiye?
questions.explanation: Overall lead-to-win = 30 ÷ 1,500 = 2%. Leads = 45 ÷ 0.02 = 2,250, option B (stage-wise: 45 ÷ (30/90) = 135 proposals, 135 ÷ 0.3 = 450 qualified, 450 ÷ 0.2 = 2,250 leads). Option C sirf 15 extra wins ke liye 15 extra leads jodta hai, jaise har lead win ho. Option D 1% conversion maan leta hai. Option A back-solve ko qualified stage par rok deta hai: 450 qualified chahiye, leads nahi.

questions.question: Fictional 'Tarang Analytics' ki pipeline: 5 deals × ₹10 lakh 'discovery' stage par (probability 20%), 3 deals × ₹15 lakh 'proposal' stage par (50%), aur 2 deals × ₹20 lakh 'negotiation' stage par (80%). Weighted pipeline kitni hai?
questions.explanation: Weighted = 50 × 0.2 + 45 × 0.5 + 40 × 0.8 = 10 + 22.5 + 32 = ₹64.5 lakh, option D. Option A unweighted total hai. Option B teeno probabilities ka simple average (50%) poori pipeline par lagata hai, jo stage-wise values ka weight ignore karta hai. Option C sirf negotiation wale deals ko poori value par ginta hai.

questions.question: Ek fictional manufacturer price objection deta hai. Vendor ka solution ₹30 lakh one-time aur ₹6 lakh per saal maintenance ka hai, aur customer ke data ke hisaab se isse ₹18 lakh per saal bachenge. Objection handle karne ke liye payback period kitna batana chahiye?
questions.explanation: Net annual saving = 18 − 6 = ₹12 lakh. Payback = 30 ÷ 12 = 2.5 saal, option D. Option A maintenance cost bhool jaata hai (30 ÷ 18), jo customer ke finance team ke saamne credibility tod deta hai. Option B one-time cost ko maintenance se divide karta hai.

questions.question: Fictional 'Nirmaan ERP' ki ek sales team ka quarterly quota ₹2 crore hai. Historical win rate (value ke hisaab se) 25% hai. Abhi open pipeline ₹5.6 crore hai. Quota realistic banane ke liye aur kitni pipeline (value) chahiye?
options: Kuch nahi; pipeline quota se 2.8 guna hai
questions.explanation: 25% win rate par ₹2 crore jeetne ke liye 2 ÷ 0.25 = ₹8 crore pipeline chahiye (4× coverage). Gap = 8 − 5.6 = ₹2.4 crore, option A. Option C expected bookings ka gap hai (5.6 × 0.25 = 1.4, 2 − 1.4 = 0.6), pipeline ka nahi; ₹0.6 crore bookings ke liye 0.6 ÷ 0.25 = ₹2.4 crore pipeline chahiye. Option B coverage ko win rate ke bina judge karta hai. Option D sirf pipeline se quota ghataata hai.

weeks.title: Negotiation, Conflict and Trust Around Data
weeks.summary: Is week aap BATNA, reservation price aur ZOPA se negotiation plan karna, common negotiation traps pehchaanna, KPI aur dashboard ownership jaise internal conflicts sambhaalna, aur data protection se trust banaana seekhoge.
concepts: **BATNA aur reservation price**: BATNA (Best Alternative To a Negotiated Agreement) = agar ye deal na hui to aapka sabse achha option. Isi se **reservation price** (walk-away point) nikalta hai: buyer ke liye maximum jo woh dega, seller ke liye minimum jo woh lega. Strong BATNA = strong negotiating position; isliye negotiation se pehle apna BATNA sudhaaro aur doosre ka estimate karo.

**ZOPA**: Zone Of Possible Agreement = seller ke reservation price aur buyer ke reservation price ke beech ka range. Agar seller ka minimum buyer ke maximum se zyada hai to ZOPA nahi hai aur deal nahi honi chahiye. Reservation price nikaalte waqt alternative ki poori cost lo: competitor ki quote + switching cost, ya seller ke liye cost + chhoda hua doosra profit.

**Distributive vs integrative**: distributive (fixed pie) negotiation mein ek issue (price) hai aur ek ka gain doosre ka loss. Integrative mein kai issues (price, contract length, payment terms, SLA, data rights) hote hain aur parties unhe alag value deti hain; **logrolling** (jo mujhe kam important, tumhe zyada, woh tumhe do) se total value badhti hai.

**Negotiation traps**: **anchoring** (pehla number baaki discussion ko kheench leta hai), **framing** (gain vs loss ki tarah present karne se risk appetite badalti hai), **escalation of commitment** (itna invest kar diya to deal kisi bhi keemat par), **winner's curse** (offer turant accept hua to shayad zyada de diya), **fixed-pie bias** (maan lena ki interests poori tarah opposite hain), aur overconfidence. Bachaav: data-backed benchmark, likha hua walk-away point, aur multi-issue offers.

**KPI aur dashboard ownership conflicts**: Sales aur Marketing ke 'qualified lead' ya 'active customer' ke alag numbers ka asli kaaran aksar alag definitions aur alag data sources hota hai. Hal: metric ki likhit definition (data dictionary), ek **data owner** (definition ka faisla) aur **data steward** (quality aur pipeline), ek single source of truth, aur badlaav ke liye change process.

**Conflict handling styles** (assertiveness × cooperativeness): competing (apni baat manwaana), accommodating (doosre ki maan lena), avoiding (taal dena), compromising (beech ka rasta, dono thoda chhodte hain) aur collaborating (milkar aisa solution jo dono ki zarooraten poori kare). Long-term relationships aur shared metrics mein collaborating best hota hai; time-critical crisis mein competing zaroori ho sakta hai.

**Data protection aur trust**: B2B deals aur partnerships mein aksar data share hota hai. India ka Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 personal data ke liye consent, **purpose limitation** (jis purpose ke liye data liya, usi ke liye use), data minimisation, security safeguards aur breach notification par zor deta hai; data jiska hai woh 'Data Principal' aur jo purpose decide karta hai woh 'Data Fiduciary'. Practical rule: sirf zaroori data, jahan ho sake aggregated ya pseudonymised, likhit data-sharing agreement ke saath.

example.problem: Fictional vendor 'Dhruv Analytics' ek data platform fictional retailer 'Sagar Retail' ko bechna chahta hai. Dhruv ka delivery cost ₹30 lakh hai, aur agar ye deal na hui to wahi team ek doosre project par ₹8 lakh profit kama sakti hai. Sagar ke paas competitor ki quote ₹46 lakh hai, jisme ₹4 lakh migration cost alag se lagega (Dhruv mein ye cost nahi). ZOPA aur ek achhi negotiation strategy nikaalo.
steps: Dhruv ka reservation price = cost ₹30 lakh + chhoda hua profit ₹8 lakh = ₹38 lakh.
Sagar ka BATNA = competitor: 46 + 4 = ₹50 lakh total, to Sagar ka reservation price ₹50 lakh.
ZOPA = ₹38 lakh se ₹50 lakh; koi bhi deal is range mein dono ke liye BATNA se behtar hai.
Dhruv ka opening offer ZOPA ke upar ke hisse mein ho sakta hai (jaise ₹49 lakh, data-backed ROI ke saath) kyunki pehla credible number anchor banta hai.
Integrative move: Sagar ke liye cash flow important hai, Dhruv ke liye lamba contract. Offer: ₹45 lakh, 3-saal contract, quarterly payments; dono ko price se zyada value milti hai.
Data clause: Dhruv model training ke liye customer-level data maangta hai; sahi offer = sirf zaroori fields, pseudonymised, likhit agreement ke saath, Sagar ke consent purposes ke andar.
Answer: **ZOPA ₹38–50 lakh**; ₹45 lakh + 3-saal contract + quarterly payment + limited, pseudonymised data sharing ek integrative deal hai.

mistakes: BATNA mein switching ya migration cost bhool jaana, jisse apna walk-away point galat (kam) nikalta hai aur achhi deal bhi chhoot jaati hai.
Doosri party ke pehle number ko 'market price' maan lena (anchoring). Negotiation se pehle apna benchmark data ready rakho aur usi se counter karo.
KPI conflict ko 'kiska number sahi hai' ki ladaai bana dena. Pehle definitions aur data sources compare karo; aksar dono numbers apni definition se sahi hote hain.
revision: BATNA → reservation price → ZOPA.
Alternative ki poori cost lo (quote + switching cost).
Integrative: multiple issues, logrolling se total value badhti hai.
Traps: anchoring, framing, escalation, winner's curse, fixed-pie.
KPI conflict: definition + owner + single source of truth.
Data: consent, purpose limitation, minimisation, agreement.

questions.question: Negotiation mein BATNA ka sahi matlab kya hai?
options: Is deal mein sabse achha price jo aapko mil sakta hai
Dono parties ke reservation prices ke beech ka range
Opening offer jo anchor ki tarah kaam kare
Agar ye deal na ho to aapke paas sabse achha alternative
questions.explanation: BATNA = Best Alternative To a Negotiated Agreement, yaani deal fail hone par aapka sabse achha option, option D. Isi se reservation price nikalta hai. Option B ZOPA ki definition hai, jo common confusion hai. Option A target ya aspiration price hai, aur option C anchoring ki baat hai.

questions.question: Fictional delivery app 'Dabba Express' ne customers ke phone numbers sirf delivery updates bhejne ke liye liye the. Ab ek partner ke saath deal mein marketing team in numbers par partner ke loan offers bhejna chahti hai, bina naye consent ke. Data protection ka kaunsa principle sabse seedha toot raha hai?
questions.explanation: Data ek specific purpose (delivery updates) ke liye liya gaya tha; naye, alag purpose (partner ke loan offers) ke liye bina consent use karna purpose limitation todta hai, option B. Option D (zaroorat se zyada samay tak data rakhna) bhi ek principle hai, par yahan problem duration nahi, use ka purpose hai. Accuracy aur portability ka is situation se seedha sambandh nahi.

questions.question: Ek software vendor ₹90 lakh 'list price' se negotiation shuru karta hai. Buyer ki team ke paas benchmark data hai ki aise solutions ₹55 lakh ke aas-paas bikte hain, phir bhi woh ₹75 lakh counter karti hai aur ₹70 lakh par deal karke khush hai ki '₹20 lakh bacha liye'. Buyer kis negotiation trap mein phansa?
questions.explanation: Vendor ka pehla number (₹90 lakh) reference point ban gaya aur buyer ne apne benchmark (₹55 lakh) ki jagah usi se counter aur 'bachat' measure ki: anchoring, option C. Option A tab hota jab buyer ka pehla offer turant accept ho jaata aur use lagta ki zyada de diya. Option B pehle se lagaye resources ki wajah se deal mein phanse rehna hai, jo yahan nahi dikhta.

questions.question: Fictional company 'Kriti Cosmetics' mein Sales dashboard 1,200 'qualified leads' dikhata hai aur Marketing dashboard 1,850. Dono teams kehti hain ki metric unka hai. Analytics head ke liye sabse achha approach kya hai?
options: Dono teams ke saath milkar ek likhit definition tay karo, ek data owner chuno, aur metric ko ek shared source of truth mein rakho
CEO se kaho ek team ka number choose kare aur doosri team ka dashboard band kare
Dono numbers dashboards par rehne do taaki koi team naraz na ho
Dono numbers ka average (1,525) official number bana do
questions.explanation: Farak ka kaaran aksar alag definitions aur sources hota hai; dono ki zarooraten samajh kar common definition, owner aur single source of truth banana collaborating approach hai jo problem ki jad theek karta hai, option A. Option D compromising hai par aisa number banata hai jo kisi definition se match nahi karta. Option C avoiding hai (confusion bani rehti hai), aur option B competing/authority se ek team ki zaroorat ignore karta hai.

questions.question: Fictional buyer 'Vardaan Hospitals' aur supplier 'MedEquip' do issues par negotiate kar rahe hain. Har option ke points neeche hain (zyada = behtar). Kaunsa combination dono ke total points maximise karta hai?
questions.code:
Issue            Option        Buyer pts   Supplier pts
Delivery         Fast (2 wk)       40            0
Delivery         Normal (6 wk)      0           10
Payment terms    60 days           20            0
Payment terms    30 days            0           50
questions.explanation: Totals: A = 40 + 20 = 60; B = 40 + 50 = 90; C = 10 + 50 = 60; D = 20 + 10 = 30. Option B sabse zyada (90): buyer ko delivery zyada important hai aur supplier ko payment terms, to har party apna kam-important issue chhodti hai (logrolling). Option A buyer ke liye best hai (60 points) par supplier ko kuch nahi deta; ye fixed-pie soch ka trap hai.

questions.question: Fictional vendor 'Prisma Data' ka ek project par delivery cost ₹32 lakh hai; deal na hui to wahi team doosre project par ₹10 lakh profit kama sakti hai. Buyer 'Unnati Retail' ke paas competitor ki quote ₹52 lakh hai, jisme ₹3 lakh switching cost alag se lagegi (Prisma mein ye cost nahi). ZOPA kya hai?
questions.explanation: Seller ka reservation price = 32 + 10 = ₹42 lakh (isse kam par doosra project behtar). Buyer ka reservation price = 52 + 3 = ₹55 lakh (competitor ki poori cost). ZOPA = ₹42–55 lakh, option D. Option B buyer ki switching cost bhool jaata hai; option C seller ke chhode hue profit (opportunity cost) ko; option A dono ko.

weeks.title: Service Failure and Recovery in B2C and B2B
weeks.summary: Is week aap service failures ke types, customers ka response, justice-based recovery, B2C aur B2B recovery ka farak (SLAs, service credits, renewals), aur organisation, employees aur customers par iske asar ko numbers se evaluate karna seekhoge.
concepts: **Service failure**: jab service customer ki expectation se neeche rahe. Types: core service failure (order hi nahi pahuncha, system down), process failure (lambi wait, galat billing), customer request handle na karna (special request ignore), aur employee ka unprompted bura behaviour. Failure ki root cause category data mein tag karo, tabhi trend dikhega.

**Customer response aur complaint iceberg**: zyada tar dissatisfied customers complain nahi karte; chupchaap switch karte hain ya negative word-of-mouth/online reviews dete hain. Agar sirf x% complain karte hain to complaints ÷ x% se asli dissatisfied customers ka estimate milta hai. Isliye complaint count ko 'problem ka size' nahi, 'problem ka sample' samjho.

**Recovery aur justice**: customer recovery ko teen tarah judge karta hai: **distributive justice** (outcome: refund, replacement, compensation), **procedural justice** (process: speed, kitni baar call karna pada, flexibility, clear policy) aur **interactional justice** (behaviour: politeness, empathy, sachchi apology, explanation). Teeno mein se ek bhi kamzor ho to recovery adhuri lagti hai.

**Service recovery paradox**: kabhi-kabhi bahut achhi recovery ke baad customer ki satisfaction aur loyalty us level se bhi upar chali jaati hai jo failure na hone par hoti. Par ye guaranteed nahi hai, aur baar-baar failure par kaam nahi karta, isliye ye 'galti karo aur sudhaaro' ki strategy nahi hai.

**B2C vs B2B recovery**: B2C mein bahut saare customers, standard scripts, fast compensation (voucher, refund) aur social media ka pressure. B2B mein contract aur **SLA** (uptime, response time) define karte hain ki kya failure hai; remedy aksar **service credit** (fee ka %), root-cause report, account team ki escalation aur kai stakeholders (users, IT, procurement) ko alag communication hoti hai. B2B mein asli risk renewal aur account expansion ka hai.

**Organisation, employees, customers**: organisation ke liye failure ka cost = lost customer lifetime value + compensation + rework + brand damage; recovery ek investment hai jiska ROI nikal sakte ho. Employees ke liye: front-line ko **empowerment** (ek limit tak bina approval compensation dena), training aur emotional labour ka support; warna burnout aur dheemi recovery. Customers ke liye: trust, effort aur future behaviour (repeat, referral, churn).

**Recovery metrics**: complaint rate, first-contact resolution, time to resolution, recovery ke baad CSAT/NPS, aur sabse important, recovered vs non-recovered customers ka churn ya repeat rate. Expected value check: (churn bina recovery − churn recovery ke saath) × affected customers × CLV, minus recovery cost.

example.problem: Fictional grocery app 'Udaan Fresh' par roz 200 orders fail hote hain (late ya missing items). Data: bina recovery ke aise 30% customers churn karte hain; agar har affected customer ko turant apology + ₹150 voucher diya jaaye to churn 10% reh jaata hai. Average customer lifetime value (margin) ₹4,000 hai. Kya recovery program worth it hai?
steps: Bina recovery expected loss = 200 × 30% × ₹4,000 = ₹2,40,000 per din.
Recovery ke saath churn loss = 200 × 10% × ₹4,000 = ₹80,000.
Recovery cost = 200 × ₹150 = ₹30,000.
Recovery ke saath total cost = ₹80,000 + ₹30,000 = ₹1,10,000.
Saath mein root cause (kis dark store ya time slot mein failures) fix karo, taaki 200 hi ghatein.
Answer: recovery program se roz lagbhag **₹1,30,000** ka expected loss bachta hai, isliye worth it hai.

mistakes: Complaint count ko dissatisfied customers ki poori sankhya maan lena. Zyada tar log complain nahi karte; complaint rate se upar scale karke estimate karo.
Recovery ko sirf compensation (distributive) samajhna. Dheema process ya rude behaviour ke saath bada voucher bhi customer ko wapas nahi laata.
B2B failure ko sirf SLA credit ka hisaab samajhna. Asli financial risk renewal aur expansion ka hai; account-level recovery plan aur root-cause report zaroori hai.
revision: Justice: distributive (outcome), procedural (process), interactional (behaviour).
Recovery paradox: achhi recovery kabhi satisfaction ko pehle se upar le jaati hai, guaranteed nahi.
Dissatisfied ≈ complaints ÷ complaint rate.
B2B: SLA, service credits, stakeholders, renewal risk.
Recovery value = churn kami × customers × CLV − recovery cost.
Front-line empowerment = tez recovery.

questions.question: Fictional restaurant chain 'Zaika' mein order galat aane par manager khud table par aakar politely sorry kehta hai, ghalti ki wajah honestly batata hai aur customer ki baat dhyaan se sunta hai. Recovery ka ye hissa kis justice dimension ko address karta hai?
questions.explanation: Politeness, empathy, sachchi apology aur explanation, yaani customer ke saath vyavhaar: interactional justice, option A. Option B tab hota jab outcome diya jaata (refund, free dish). Option C process ki fairness aur speed hai. Option D justice dimension hi nahi, recovery ka ek possible result hai.

questions.question: 'Service recovery paradox' ka sabse sahi matlab kya hai?
options: Service failure ke baad customers hamesha switch kar jaate hain
Jitna bada compensation, utni zyada loyalty, bina kisi limit ke
Jo customers complain nahi karte, woh satisfied hote hain
Bahut achhi recovery ke baad kuch customers ki satisfaction us level se bhi upar ja sakti hai jo failure na hone par hoti
questions.explanation: Paradox yahi hai ki failure + excellent recovery kabhi-kabhi no-failure se bhi zyada satisfaction deta hai, option D; ye guaranteed nahi aur baar-baar failure par kaam nahi karta. Option B trap hai: compensation ka asar limited hai aur process aur behaviour bhi chahiye. Option C complaint iceberg ki ulti galatfahmi hai.

questions.question: Fictional cloud provider 'Akash Hosting' ka ek B2B client ₹6,00,000 per month deta hai. SLA: monthly uptime 99.9% ya zyada par koi credit nahi; 99.0% se 99.9% se kam tak 10% credit; 99.0% se kam par 25% credit. 30-din ke mahine mein total downtime 300 minutes raha. Client ko kitna service credit milega?
questions.explanation: Mahine mein 30 × 24 × 60 = 43,200 minutes. Uptime = 1 − 300 ÷ 43,200 ≈ 99.31%, jo 99.0% aur 99.9% ke beech hai: 10% credit = ₹60,000, option C. Option D downtime ke minutes ka pro-rata fee hai, SLA ka slab nahi. Option B 25% slab lagata hai (300 minutes ko zyada bada samajh kar), aur option A 99.31% ko 99.9% se upar padh leta hai.

questions.question: Fictional electronics brand 'Volt' ke ek naye earphone model par mahine mein 120 complaints aayi. Industry research ke hisaab se sirf 4% dissatisfied customers formally complain karte hain. Is mahine is model ke dissatisfied customers ka estimate kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Complaints sirf 4% dissatisfied customers se aati hain: 120 ÷ 0.04 = 3,000 dissatisfied customers, option B. Option D (3,000 − 120) sirf woh log hain jinhone complain nahi kiya, kul dissatisfied nahi. Option C 120 × 4% hai, ulta calculation. Option A 120 mein sirf 4% jod deta hai (120 × 1.04 ≈ 125).

questions.question: Fictional food delivery app 'Thali Express' par roz 300 orders late ya galat jaate hain. Bina recovery ke inme se 25% customers churn karte hain; har affected customer ko turant apology + ₹100 voucher dene par churn 10% reh jaata hai. Average customer lifetime value (margin) ₹3,000 hai. Voucher ka kharcha ghataake, recovery program se roz kitna expected nuksaan bachta hai?
questions.explanation: Bina recovery: 300 × 25% × 3,000 = ₹2,25,000. Recovery ke saath: 300 × 10% × 3,000 = ₹90,000 churn loss + 300 × 100 = ₹30,000 vouchers = ₹1,20,000. Bachat = 2,25,000 − 1,20,000 = ₹1,05,000, option C. Option A voucher ka cost ghataana bhool jaata hai. Option D bina recovery wala poora loss hai, bachat nahi.

questions.question: Fictional IT services firm 'Sankalp Tech' ke ek B2B account se ₹40 lakh revenue aur ₹12 lakh margin per saal aata hai. Ek bade outage ke baad, bina recovery ke contract renewal ki probability 50% hai. ₹3 lakh ka recovery program (service credit + dedicated engineer + root-cause report) renewal probability 80% kar deta hai. Agle saal ke expected margin ke hisaab se kya recovery program karna chahiye?
options: Haan; expected margin ₹9 lakh zyada hai
Nahi; renewal phir bhi pakka nahi, isliye ₹3 lakh waste hai
Haan; expected margin ₹3.6 lakh zyada hai
questions.explanation: Bina recovery: 50% × 12 = ₹6 lakh. Recovery ke saath: 80% × 12 − 3 = ₹6.6 lakh. Farak ₹0.6 lakh = ₹60,000, option A. Option B margin ki jagah revenue lagata hai (30% × 40 − 3). Option D recovery ka ₹3 lakh cost bhool jaata hai. Option C expected value ki jagah 'pakka' outcome maangta hai; probability badhna hi value hai.
